scenes.heading: Creative writing
scenes.sub: Hook them early, show the feeling, finish strong
scenes.say: Markers read lots of stories on the same prompt. The ones that stand out hook the reader early, make them feel something, and have a real ending. Here's how to write one of those.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A movie trailer starts with action, not opening credits
scenes.science: A test story starts in the middle of the action
scenes.breaks: a trailer can jump around; your story still needs a clear order and a proper ending.
scenes.say: Think of a movie trailer. It doesn't start with the credits. It starts with something happening. Your story should too. Skip the alarm clock and breakfast, and begin right in the middle of the action.

scenes.heading: Show, don't tell
scenes.say: Next, show, don't tell. Jai was nervous tells the reader. Jai wiped his sweaty palms on his shorts again shows it. When the reader works out the feeling, they feel it too.

scenes.heading: Build the scene
points: Keep the same tense and point of view
scenes.say: To build a scene, use at least two senses, not just sight. Use short sentences to speed things up and longer ones to slow down. And keep the same tense and point of view all the way through.

scenes.heading: Pick the best ending
scenes.question: Tom is scared to play piano at the school concert. Which ending works best?
scenes.say: Tom is scared to play piano at the concert. A dream ending cancels the story. Becoming world famous is unbelievable. The best ending: he plays, makes two mistakes, sees his little sister clapping, and realises that's all he needed. It settles his fear in a believable way.

points: Start in the middle of the action
scenes.say: Quick recap. Start in the middle of the action. Show feelings through actions and details. Use your senses and vary your sentences. And end by settling the problem, never with a dream. Now try the practice questions!
